name: room
text: Room opened — goal: visualization: Own the VISUAL PRESENTATION of the interface — visibility, liveliness, clarity, enjoyment

name: Facet
text: We should create a high-contrast color scheme for the interface to improve visibility. This decision is best because it will help users quickly distinguish between different elements, reducing eye strain and making the interface more enjoyable to use. By choosing a high-contrast color scheme, we're accepting the trade-off of potentially limiting our brand's ability to use subtle, nuanced colors. This trade-off is worth it, as clarity and usability should take priority over aesthetic preferences in this case.

name: Pane
text: High-contrast colors improve visibility but risk alienating users with visual impairments or those sensitive to bright hues. A better alternative is adaptive contrast—let users toggle between high and low contrast modes. Settle it with A/B testing: measure task completion time and user-reported comfort across both schemes.
